overview:
This check monitors [Apache NiFi][1] through the Datadog Agent.

Apache NiFi is a data integration and automation platform for moving data between systems. This integration uses the NiFi REST API to collect JVM health, flow throughput, queue backpressure, processor status, and bulletin events, and it collects application logs from `nifi-app.log`. Together, this data provides visibility into data pipeline health without requiring NiFi-side configuration.

[1]: https://nifi.apache.org/
setup:
Follow the instructions below to install and configure this check for an Agent running on a host. For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][3] for guidance on applying these instructions.

### Installation

The NiFi check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package.
No additional installation is needed on your server.

### Configuration

1. Edit the `nifi.d/conf.yaml` file, in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory to start collecting your NiFi performance data. See the [sample nifi.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

2. At minimum, configure the `api_url`, `username`, and `password`:

   ```yaml
   instances:
     - api_url: https://localhost:8443/nifi-api
       username: <NIFI_USERNAME>
       password: <NIFI_PASSWORD>
       tls_verify: true
   ```

3. [Restart the Agent][5].

### Log collection

1. Collecting logs is disabled by default in the Datadog Agent. Enable it in your `datadog.yaml` file:

   ```yaml
   logs_enabled: true
   ```

2. Add the following configuration block to your `nifi.d/conf.yaml` file to start collecting your NiFi logs:

   ```yaml
   logs:
     - type: file
       path: /opt/nifi/logs/nifi-app.log
       source: nifi
       service: nifi
   ```

   Change the `path` and `service` parameter values based on your environment. See the [sample nifi.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

3. Optional: Configure NiFi to include a UTC offset in its log timestamps. By default, NiFi writes local time without a timezone, so the integration keeps that time in the `nifi.local_time` attribute and dates each log by when Datadog received it. To date logs by the time NiFi wrote them, edit `conf/logback.xml` in your NiFi installation and set the pattern of the `APP_FILE` appender to:

   ```xml
   <pattern>%date{"yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss,SSSXXX"} %level [%thread] %logger{40} %msg%n</pattern>
   ```

   Keep the quotes around the date format. Without them, logback reads the text after the comma as a timezone ID and NiFi starts without any logging. Restart NiFi to apply the change.

4. [Restart the Agent][5].

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][6] and look for `nifi` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: nifi.can_connect
metrics.description: Whether the check can reach and authenticate with the NiFi API. 1 = reachable 0 = unreachable.

metrics.name: nifi.cluster.connected_node_count
metrics.description: Number of nodes currently connected to the cluster.

metrics.name: nifi.cluster.is_healthy
metrics.description: Whether all cluster nodes are connected. 1 = all connected 0 = degraded.

metrics.name: nifi.cluster.total_node_count
metrics.description: Total number of nodes in the cluster.

metrics.name: nifi.connection.flowfiles_in
metrics.description: FlowFiles into this connection during snapshot window.

metrics.name: nifi.connection.flowfiles_out
metrics.description: FlowFiles out of this connection during snapshot window.

metrics.name: nifi.connection.queued_bytes
metrics.description: Bytes currently queued in this connection.

metrics.name: nifi.connection.queued_count
metrics.description: FlowFiles currently queued in this connection.

metrics.name: nifi.flow.bytes_queued
metrics.description: Total bytes queued across all connections.

metrics.name: nifi.flow.flowfiles_queued
metrics.description: Total FlowFiles queued across all connections.

monitors.title: NiFi API is unreachable
monitors.description: Alerts when the Agent cannot reach or authenticate with the NiFi REST API (nifi.can_connect stays 0), which means NiFi telemetry stops being collected for the affected host.

monitors.title: NiFi cluster is degraded
monitors.description: Alerts when a monitored NiFi instance reports that one or more cluster nodes have disconnected from the cluster coordinator (nifi.cluster.is_healthy = 0). This metric is emitted only in clustered mode, so the monitor ignores missing data and never fires for standalone deployments.

monitors.title: NiFi processors are in an invalid state
monitors.description: Counts NiFi processors in the Invalid run status. They have incomplete or inconsistent configuration (such as a missing required property or a disabled Controller Service) and cannot run until fixed. Alerts only on sustained invalid states, not brief ones during flow updates.
